comparison: Perfect alignment on validation limitations (C166-C174). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the authors' acknowledgment that PSTH dominates similarity scores and that multiple neurons can have high similarity. OpenEval notes this as 'honest and critical self-assessment' while peer reviewers implicitly accept it as 'thorough methodological discussion.'

Strong agreement on the statistical approach for threshold selection (C114-C120, C127-C129, C187-C191). Both evaluations support the mixture model fitting and recognition that reference units are not representative. OpenEval explicitly validates the Monte Carlo simulation while peer reviewers accept it as part of 'generally sound and properly tested' methodology.

Complete agreement on main performance results (C9-C10, C150-C153). Both affirm the reported accuracy metrics. OpenEval notes 'clearly stated with specific percentages' while peer reviewers state the approach 'performs quite well, with a high proportion of neurons accurately matched across multiple weeks.'

Divergent evaluations on drift correction demonstration (C89-C95, C106). OpenEval finds the approach 'justified' and 'validates the method,' acknowledging the slight difference between imposed (12μm) and estimated (15.65μm) drift. Peer reviewers express 'confusion about the point of the imposed drift and how the value of 12μm is chosen,' requesting clarification.

Agreement on long-term tracking results (C136-C138, C142-C143, C146-C147). Both accept the categorization into three chain types and the observation that loss rates are similar. OpenEval provides detailed validation while peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of overall positive assessment.

Agreement on validation strategy using visual receptive fields (C8, C61-C62, C75, C107-C109, C165, C209). Both accept this approach as appropriate ground truth. OpenEval notes it 'follows established practice' while peer reviewers affirm 'they used the visual receptive fields...as ground truth' without questioning the strategy.

Strong agreement on core methodological innovation (C5-C7, C45-C46, C64-C65, C67-C68, C148, C206-C208). Both find the two-stage EMD approach well-motivated and properly validated. OpenEval notes 'detailed methods and experimental validation' while peer reviewers describe it as 'generally sound and properly tested' and 'important.'

Overlapping positive assessment of algorithmic approach (C59-C70, C206-C219 for OpenEval; C5, C7, C45-C46, C64-C65, C67-C68, C148, C206-C208 for peer). Both support the core EMD procedure and use of spatial/waveform information. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation while peer reviewers affirm overall soundness.

Agreement on practical considerations and recommendations (C199-C205). Both accept the discussion of spike sorting reliability limitations and recommendations for future use. OpenEval finds recommendations 'practical and well-reasoned' while peer reviewers accept them as 'appropriate methodological transparency.'

Divergent focus on dataset description and generalizability (C51-C58, C236-C243 for OpenEval; C51-C53, C179-C180, C236, C240 for peer). OpenEval supports the experimental dataset description as 'clear' and 'appropriate.' Peer reviewers express 'significant concern about generalizability,' noting the study only examines 'one brain area, one species, one spike sorter, one behavioral prep.'

Divergent evaluation of generalization procedures (C182-C183, C192-C196). OpenEval finds the procedures 'detailed' and recommendations 'appropriate.' Peer reviewers note 'no validation of those generalizations was done using data from different experimental conditions,' representing a 'significant limitation.'

Divergent assessment of technical implementation details (C76-C77, C222-C226 for OpenEval; C68, C77, C207 for peer). OpenEval supports the adaptation and weighting choices as 'appropriate and well-justified.' Peer reviewers question the weighting scheme, asking how performance is affected by different weightings and noting w=1500 suggests 'only the waveform distance matter.'

Agreement on similarity of tracked unit types (C63, C155 for OpenEval; C63, C134, C154, C158 for peer). Both accept that reference units are representative of all tracked units. OpenEval validates statistical tests while peer reviewers highlight the importance of tracking 'without relying on matching neural receptive fields.'

Agreement on practical advantages (C148-C149, C156-C158 for OpenEval; C156-C157, C199-C205 for peer). Both accept the simplicity of single-pass sorting and choice of Kilosort. OpenEval notes these as 'practical advantage' and 'well-justified' while peer reviewers implicitly value the simplicity.

Partial overlap on validation approach (C107-C109, C256-C276 for OpenEval; C8, C61-C62, C75, C107-C109, C165, C209 for peer). Both support the use of visual receptive fields for validation. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of criteria and statistical tests while peer reviewers accept the overall strategy.

OpenEval supports the distance thresholding approach (C83-C84, C99-C103, C110-C113, C221) as 'critical methodological component' with appropriate iterative refinement. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific aspect.

OpenEval supports the observed trend of decreasing reference unit fraction over time (C175-C178) with 'plausible explanations' and 'appropriate interpretation of limitations.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific observation.

OpenEval supports the quality control approach for detecting problematic datasets (C159-C164), finding the exclusion of AL036 datasets 1-2 'appropriate and well-justified' based on statistical evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports the comparison to prior methods (C244-C255), finding the description of Steinmetz et al. 2021 'accurate' and the comparison 'fair.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific comparison.

OpenEval supports background and motivation claims (C1-C4, C11-C16) as 'well-established' and 'accurately describe the scientific context.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these introductory claims.

OpenEval supports claims about field challenges (C21-C44) as 'accurately describe known challenges' with 'appropriate citations.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background claims about technical problems.
